newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sterling/mark drifts down in late Asian trading.
newsitem.headline: Sterling/mark drifts down in late Asian trading.

text.p: Sterling was drifting lower on the mark in in late Asian trading as traders took profits after its sharp rise following the U.K. budget on Wednesday.
At 0623 GMT it was trading at 2.9315/25 marks in Singapore after touching 2.9427 with cable at $1.6732/42 after 1.6780. Initial indications from Europe also had it trading below the highs.
Sterling shot up in response to Finance Minister Gordon Brown's first budget which although tight on the fiscal front, was not seen as tight enough to prevent a near-term rise in interest rates.
There is speculation the Bank of England will raise interest rates to help dampen the British economy at the next scheduled meeting of the monetary policy council next week.
"It was a good rise and when people here saw that Europe wasn't going to take it any further some took profits," said one trader. "It looks like it may drift a bit lower in Europe today."
